300.author: wyhohyw
300.body:
﻿Daily CI gave RACE and FACT one shared 10-minute deadline. RACE finished, then the judge was killed while citation checking was still running, so citation accuracy and verification coverage were never recorded. On the 13 and 14 October nightlies every DRB case showed this. Forty minutes covers those runs except a DRB-64 report that cites the same manuals as dozens of distinct statements; thirty minutes still clips that report and leaves only about three minutes of margin on the next-slowest cases.

## Evaluation deadline
`.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml` sets `E2E_DRB_EVAL_TIMEOUT_MS` to `2400000`. The local default stays one hour. The DeepResearchBench README's daily evaluation budget matches this deadline. Research shard jobs remain capped at 240 minutes, so the longer judge fits inside the job.

## Validation
`pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run. This commit changes a nightly workflow constant and its README; those layers do not execute the real DRB judge. WSL on this machine has bubblewrap, but the fresh worktree has no `node_modules`, and installing it would not observe the 40-minute deadline. The check is the next nightly after this merges and syncs to GitHub: each DRB case should record citation accuracy and verification coverage instead of `running`.

## E2E user journeys
Not applicable. No UI, API, CLI, or session behavior changes. Delivery assertions are unchanged; only the separate judge deadline in daily CI is longer.
300.head: codex/drb-eval-40m
300.title: ci: allow DRB citation scoring forty minutes

302.author: wyhohyw
302.body:
Re-running a job left the previous attempt's artifact in place. Coverage then downloaded that older package by name and failed a passed UT, because the manifest still said the first attempt failed. Closes #301.

## What changes

`actions/upload-artifact@v4` keeps an existing artifact unless `overwrite` is true. On PR #295, run 38526631198, the failed UT uploaded `ut-coverage` (`status: FAIL`, 3821/3822). The re-run passed and uploaded a second package with the same name. Coverage ran with `needs.ut.result=success` and read the 07:30 package, so `scripts/coverage-report.mjs` reported incomplete coverage.

Uploads that a later job downloads by exact name now replace the previous attempt:

- `ut-coverage`
- `st-coverage`
- `mocked-e2e-plan`
- `real-e2e-plan`

`.ci/ci-contract.test.mjs` fails if a workflow downloads an artifact by exact name and the matching upload omits `overwrite: true`.

## Validation

- WSL, `node --test --test-name-pattern "latest attempt" .ci/ci-contract.test.mjs`: 1 passed, 0 failed.
- `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run. This change is GitHub Actions artifact metadata. Those layers do not observe the artifact store, and the contract test is what locks the flag.

## E2E user journeys

Not applicable. No product UI, API, CLI, or run path changes. The bug is which artifact a later GitHub Actions job downloads after a job re-run.
302.head: fix/ci-coverage-artifact-rerun
302.title: fix(ci): replace artifacts from a previous job attempt

303.author: zhaozhaozz
303.body:
Chat Completions responses can contain zero-filled `input_tokens` / `output_tokens` compatibility fields alongside valid `prompt_tokens` / `completion_tokens`. The model client preferred those aliases, so a response reporting 30,393 prompt tokens and 84 completion tokens was persisted as zero output tokens.

Use one shared usage normalizer with the actual request protocol. Chat Completions prefers prompt/completion; Responses and Anthropic prefer input/output. Aliases are fallbacks, not additional tokens. Explicit counts, including zero and counts that disagree with the reported total, are preserved; reasoning tokens are never added again. Without protocol context, conflicting positive aliases are resolved using a complete pair matching the total when possible, and the result retains conflict diagnostics.

API session naming, paper vision, and evolution accounting now share the same Chat rules. Incomplete paper usage remains unknown instead of fabricating zero counts. The adapter consumes normalized internal usage events, and the metering proxy already uses the correct Chat precedence; neither needs a rule change. E2E assertions and research-delivery behavior are unchanged.

## Validation

Tested commit: `c85c3cf8874a7571b47ea66e17d71209916efba1`, based on `bb356a3f474ee6382f05420b3cf05e24d60a756e`.

- New normalization regression matrix: 5 of 12 cases failed before the fix; all pass after it.
- Focused model/API tests: 68 passed, 0 failed.
- `pnpm typecheck`: passed.
- `pnpm ci:l1`: planned 4 / executed 4 / passed 4.
- `pnpm ci:ut`: planned 3,826 / executed 3,826 / passed 3,826, 0 failed or skipped, JiuwenSwarm backend.
- `pnpm ci:st`: planned 3 / executed 3 / passed 3; SDK contract sub-suite: 66 passed plus 3 subtests.
- `pnpm ci:e2e`: planned 74 / executed 74 / passed 74, 0 failed or skipped; 9 additional JiuwenSwarm checks passed.

## E2E user journeys

PASS — isolated production API and Runner CLIs, with a local provider stub, tested with both native and JiuwenSwarm executors. For each backend, five scenarios each complete a reply, query the persisted public `/usage` result, and continue the same session: 20 completed Runs in total. The observed input/output/total tuples are `30393/84/30477`, `10/7/19`, `10/0/10`, and `8/5/13` for both Responses and Anthropic. Repeated cumulative usage frames do not increase the totals.

The paid real-provider L3 suite was not rerun. The reported conflicting fields were replayed deterministically through both product executors; no E2E assertion was weakened.

## Release

Release category: release:fix

New model calls record usage according to their API dialect. No configuration or storage migration is required; historical usage records are not rewritten.
303.head: fix/api-dialect-token-usage
303.title: fix(model): prefer protocol token fields over conflicting aliases
